In code review comment: https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/sky-ntt-migration/pull/3#discussion_r2238671684

@oldchili has asked for introduction of support https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-foundry-upgrades/tree/main

to fulfill this goal, this PR:
- upgrades forge-std to 1.9.5
- upgrades openzeppelin-contracts to 4.9.0
- reintroduces old implementation for comparison

Command to run check:
```
forge script script/SimulateNttManagerUpgrade.s.sol --rpc-url https://0xrpc.io/eth --ffi --build-info --extra-output storageLayout --force

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a complete Waiting Room system for the interview platform, providing a structured pre-interview workflow with candidate approval and host management capabilities. ## Overview The Waiting Room system manages the entire pre-interview experience from candidate arrival to interview start, featuring role-based access control, real-time event handling, and comprehensive accessibility support. ## Key Features Implemented ### 🏗️ Modular Architecture - **Event-driven state management** with pure functional reducers and discriminated union events - **Transport abstraction layer** enabling easy swapping between mock and WebSocket implementations - **Hook-based state management** (`useWaitingRoom`) with derived state and actions - **Component composition** with clear single responsibilities ### 🎭 Role-Based Experience - **Host Interface**: Candidate management table with approve/reject controls, interview start functionality - **Candidate Interface**: Join form with validation, real-time status updates, approval workflow - **Dynamic UI rendering** based on user role and current room phase ### ♿ Accessibility First (WCAG 2.1 AA) - **ARIA live regions** for dynamic status announcements to screen readers - **Focus management utilities** with automatic focus movement on form interactions - **Color-independent indicators** using text + icons + color for status communication - **Accessible table semantics** with proper headers and row/column associations - **Keyboard navigation** support throughout all interactive elements ### 🔄 Event-Driven State Machine Four distinct phases with automatic transitions: 1. `waiting_host` - Host not present yet 2. `gathering_candidates` - Host present, collecting candidate requests 3. `ready_to_start` - Approved candidates ready, can start interview 4. `in_progress` - Interview has started, transitions to main interface ### 🚪 Interview Gating The main interview interface only mounts after the `interview_started` event, preventing premature access to interview tools and ensuring proper workflow progression. ## Technical Implementation ### Core Components (`apps/interview-ui/src/components/waiting-room/`) - `WaitingRoom.tsx` - Main orchestrator with phase-driven rendering - `RoomHeader.tsx` - Interview info display with participant counts - `CandidateJoinForm.tsx` - Form validation with accessibility features - `CandidateStatusPanel.tsx` - Visual status feedback with live announcements - `HostControls.tsx` - Candidate management with accessible table interface - `ParticipantList.tsx` - Clean participant display with status indicators - `EventFeed.tsx` - Real-time activity log with human-readable descriptions ### State Management (`apps/interview-ui/src/state/`) ```typescript // Comprehensive type system with discriminated unions type WaitingRoomEvent = HostJoinedEvent | CandidateApprovedEvent | InterviewStartedEvent | ... // Pure functional reducer with invariant validation function applyEvent(snapshot: WaitingRoomSnapshot, event: WaitingRoomEvent): WaitingRoomSnapshot // Automatic phase derivation based on business rules function deriveGlobalPhase(snapshot: WaitingRoomSnapshot): WaitingRoomPhase ``` ### Transport Layer (`apps/interview-ui/src/transport/`) Clean abstraction enabling development and production implementations: - `MockWaitingRoomTransport` - Realistic simulation with auto host joining and mock candidates - `WebSocketWaitingRoomTransport` - Placeholder for backend integration ### App Integration Updated `App.tsx` with: - URL parameter parsing for interview ID and role detection (`?interview=id&role=host`) - Conditional rendering: Waiting Room → Interview Interface after start - Development controls for role switching and testing ## Mock Transport Demo The mock transport provides a realistic development experience: - Host automatically joins after 1-3 seconds - Three mock candidates (Alice, Bob, Carol) request to join with staggered timing - Complete event sourcing with activity feed - Demonstrates full approval workflow and interview start ## Accessibility Features **Screen Reader Support:** ```jsx
Interview room {interviewId}. Host is {hostPresent ? 'present' : 'not present'}. {approvedCount} approved, {pendingCount} pending candidates.
``` **Focus Management:** ```typescript // Automatic focus on form errors if (errors.name) { focusOnRef(nameInputRef); } ``` **Accessible Button Labels:** ```typescript // Context-aware button text for screen readers aria-label="Approve Alice Smith (currently pending)" ``` ## Code Quality - **TypeScript strict mode** with no implicit anys - **Exhaustive switch statements** with never assertions - **Comprehensive JSDoc documentation** with @future and #TODO markers - **Invariant validation** with structured console warnings - **Modular exports** with barrel files for clean imports ## Usage Navigate to interview rooms with URL parameters: ``` http://localhost:5173/?interview=your-interview-id&role=host http://localhost:5173/?interview=your-interview-id&role=candidate ``` Role switching available via development controls in the header. ## Documentation Updates - Enhanced `README.md` with waiting room section and usage instructions - Updated `TODO.md` with backend integration tasks and security considerations - Comprehensive inline documentation with future enhancement markers ## Next Steps The system is architected for seamless backend integration: 1. Replace mock transport with WebSocket implementation 2. Connect to interview-bff WebSocket endpoint (`/ws/interview`) 3. Add authentication and session management 4. Implement event persistence and replay functionality This implementation provides a solid foundation for the interview platform's waiting room experience with production-ready architecture and comprehensive accessibility support. > [!WARNING] > >

author: jsvd
body:
* OpenSSL 3 compatibility: stop relying on negative/zero -days for expired cert fixtures (rejected by OpenSSL 3, preventing local running of tests on MacOS). Synthesize an expired self‑signed cert at runtime in the test helper
* TLS 1.3 interop: work around mTLS handshake timeouts with JRuby on JDK 21 by disabling TLSv1.3 on the WEBrick SSL test server
* PKCS#8 key parsing: do not chomp decoded DER. Trimming binary DER can remove trailing newline bytes and corrupt the key, causing InvalidKeySpecException (covered by an existing test)

author: rahulkarajgikar
body:
### Summary

- Root cause: Next.js upgrade changed standalone output layout and root inference, breaking our launcher and asset paths for
the global install.
- Fix: Make path discovery and packaging robust to Next.js layouts; stabilize output root; harden CI so broken builds don’t
publish.

### What Broke

- Next.js 15.5.x + experimental.externalDir: true and multiple lockfiles caused:
    - Different server entry paths: .next/standalone/src/app/webui/server.js (and sometimes nested like .next/standalone/
Projects/dexto/src/app/webui/server.js).
    - Our code expected only .next/standalone/server.js.
- Packaging only copied static/ and public/ at the standalone root, not next to nested server.js. When Next started from a
nested server directory, CSS and assets weren’t found → unstyled UI.
- CI allowed publishing even when build failed (continue-on-error: true), so broken artifacts could ship.

### Changes

- Runtime launcher (src/app/web.ts):
    - Probes both known server locations; if not found, recursively searches under .next/standalone, preferring **/src/app/
webui/server.js, then any server.js.
    - Uses the discovered path or webui/server.js if present.
    - Uses the discovered path or webui/server.js if present.

- Packaged launcher (scripts/copy-webui-dist.ts generated dist/src/app/webui/server.js):
    - Same robust resolution (candidates + recursive search) with clear error messages.
    - Copies static/ and public/ to standalone root and mirrors them (plus key .next manifests) into each discovered server
directory so assets resolve regardless of nesting.

- Next.js config (src/app/webui/next.config.ts):
    - Set outputFileTracingRoot to the repo root to avoid Next inferring /Users/<user> as root, which created the “Projects/
dexto” nested standalone structure.

- Packaging/CI:
    - package.json: add prepack: "npm run build" to guarantee building WebUI + dist before any publish.
    - .github/workflows/publish.yml: remove continue-on-error on build so publish fails on build errors.

### Why This Works

- Path resolution now handles both legacy and new layouts, plus any nested variants.
- Assets and manifests are colocated with every server.js Next might emit, so CSS/JS load correctly.
- CI can’t publish a broken package, and prepack ensures builds happen for any publish path.

### Validation

- Local build and global install from .tgz:
    - npm run build && npm pack && npm install -g <tgz> → dexto --mode web launches.
    - UI loads with styling; no “Cannot find module … standalone/server.js” errors.
- Verified final install structure includes dist/src/app/webui/server.js and .next/standalone with assets and manifests.

### Impact

- Fixes fresh installs failing to start Web UI and unstyled UI on global installs.
- More resilient to future Next.js standalone layout changes.
- Slightly increases packaging step complexity; negligible size increase.

### Risks / Mitigations

- Future Next.js changes: recursive search + asset mirroring mitigate most struct changes.
- Multiple lockfiles: outputFileTracingRoot stabilizes output paths; we still keep externalDir: true for our aliasing needs.

### How To Test

- npm ci && npm run build
- npm pack && npm uninstall -g dexto && npm install -g ./*dexto*.tgz
- Run: dexto --mode web → visit http://localhost:3000
- Confirm UI is styled and functional.

### Release Notes

- fix(webui): Resolve Next standalone path regressions; ensure assets load in global installs.
- ci: Enforce build before publish and run prepack to avoid shipping broken packages.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

- Bug Fixes
  - More reliable production web UI startup across Next.js layouts/versions.
  - Each server instance now includes required assets and manifests to reduce missing-file errors.
  - Clearer diagnostics when the production server entry cannot be located; startup now fails loudly if unresolved.

- Chores
  - Publishing pipeline now blocks on a successful build; releases require a passing build.
  - Added automatic prepack build step to ensure packaged artifacts are up to date.

- Refactor
  - Improved path resolution, per-server asset replication, and output tracing to produce more stable, portable standalone builds.

body:
## Add Basic Functionalities to GraphFlow

This PR introduces the foundational components required for the initial version of GraphFlow, a node-based graph editor built with Qt/QML and C++. The following major features and files are included:

### Highlights

- **Core Models and Controller:**
  - `FlowNodeModel`: Manages nodes, their properties, positions, and attributes.
  - `FlowLinkModel`: Manages connections/links between nodes.
  - `GraphController`: Handles selection, deletion, serialization (save/load), and overall graph operations.
  - `NodeLibraryModel`: Loads node definitions from JSON and provides filtering for node selection UI.

- **QML UI Components:**
  - Modular QML files for key graph editor elements:
    - `Node.qml`, `Attribute.qml`, `Socket.qml`, `Cable.qml`, `Link.qml`
    - `Graph.qml`, `GraphFlowScene.qml`, `SelectionRect.qml`, `Background.qml`
    - `NodeList.qml` for searchable node library sidebar
    - `Theme.qml` for color palette and theming
    - `Main.qml` for window layout and app entry

- **Build System and Formatting:**
  - `CMakeLists.txt` for project setup and QML module integration.
  - Pre-commit configuration: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.clang-format`, `.cmake-format.yaml`, `.qmlformat.ini` for code style and quality.

- **Assets and Data:**
  - SVG icons for node types.
  - Example node definitions in `ui/data/nodes.json`.

- **Persistence:**
  - Graph state is automatically saved to and loaded from `lastFlow.json`.

### Usage

- Drag nodes from the sidebar onto the graph canvas.
- Connect nodes using sockets/cables.
- Select, move, and delete nodes.
- Zoom and pan the graph view.
- Node library is searchable and filterable.

### Next Steps

- Implement node execution logic (currently stubbed).
- Add more node types and extensibility.
- Unit tests and more advanced UI features.

---

**This PR lays the groundwork for further development and user-facing features.**

author: rgregnanin
body:
Questa Pull Request introduce una nuova pipeline di validazione per le PR, sostituendo quella precedente. 
L'obiettivo principale è ottimizzare l'esecuzione dei test e dei lint, migliorando l'efficienza complessiva del processo.

Cambiamenti Principali:
Ottimizzazione della validazione con lo `sharding`: La nuova pipeline introduce lo sharding per i job di lint e test. Questo significa che i pacchetti del monorepo vengono divisi in 10 shard, ed ogni shard viene eseguito su un runner separato in parallelo.

Vantaggi: Questa strategia riduce drasticamente il tempo di esecuzione complessivo della pipeline, poiché i job di lint e test vengono eseguite simultaneamente su più macchine.

Rimozione temporanea del job check: c'è un problema sulla PR [ci-test-improvements](https://github.com/pagopa/interop-be-monorepo/pull/2131) che non ho ancora avuto modo di risolvere, ma per lo scopo della PR il check non è bloccante.

Refactor delle configurazioni di Vitest: Ho riscontrato problemi di risoluzione degli import all'interno della nuova pipeline, che non si manifestavano nella CI precedente. In particolare, gli import relativi a `pagopa-interop-commons-test`, `pagopa-interop-models` e i file generati `../gen` non vengono correttamente risolti da `Vitest`.

Causa: Non mi è ben chiaro perchè ci sia questa differenza ma il mio pensiero è che la pipeline precedente, probabilmente, riusciva a dedurre i percorsi corretti, mentre la nuova, per qualche motivo, ha una gestione più rigida o differente.
@micdes-pagopa @micheledellipaoli-pagopa 

Soluzione (forse):  Per risolvere il problema, è stato necessario centralizzare la configurazione di `Vitest`  aggiungendo un file `vitest.config.ts` al livello di `root` del progetto. All'interno di questo file, una sezione `resolve alias` è stata configurata per mappare esplicitamente i percorsi dei pacchetti sopra citati. Questo assicura che il linter e il test runner possano trovare correttamente i moduli importati.
Questo ha portato anche ad eseguire il lint sui file `.test.ts`

Come suggerito [qui](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/72468249/vitest-src-folder-alias-not-resolved-in-test-files) anche il problema che si sta verificando in questo momento sarebbe risolvibile, basterebbe modificare gli import utilizzando l'alias `@`  ma non è una soluzione appetibile secondo me.
Sono aperto a suggerimenti

Inoltre, tutti i file di configurazione di Vitest all'interno dei singoli pacchetti sono stati modificati per estendere questa configurazione root (mergeConfig). Questo centralizza la gestione degli alias e garantisce una coerenza a livello di progetto.

author: thomaseizinger
body:
Unfortunately, it isn't very easy to detect whether a socket supports GSO on Linux. Hence, `quinn-udp` simply probes for its support by trying to send GSO batches and effectively disables GSO by setting the `max-gso-segments` state variable to 1 if it encounters either EINVAL (-22) or EIO (-5).

For EINVAL, `quinn-udp` has an internal retry mechanism. For EIO, the `Transmit` which is passed to `quinn-udp` needs to be re-chunked and thus cannot be automatically retried.

In order to avoid dropping packets, we therefore add a once-off retry step to sending a datagram whenever we hit EIO on Linux or Android. If the error was due to GSO not being supported, the 2nd attempt should be successful and going forward, even the first one should be until we roam the socket (where this state variable gets reset).

These packet drops have been causing flakiness in CI ever since we merged the eBPF tests. Those disable checksum offloading which appears to trigger these errors.

author: brightprogrammer
body:
Formatted reading now better detects the length of content to be parsed. Before attempting to read value at a placeholder, it'll first find the maximum possible length of reading that. This works by the following logic :

- If there are two placeholders, and nothing is between them, the first placeholder can read as much as possible, and second placeholder may get empty!
- If there are two placeholders, and there's something in between them, first placeholder can only read up until the content between the space between the placeholders. So for `{} {}`, first placeholder can only read up until first space. Then rest becomes possible read length of second placeholder.
- If there is only one placeholder, it'll get to read the whole string. It may or may not read it completely.

This new logic makes fmt reading much more helpful and easy to work with. This means more string format checking when parsing input. Pair this with the new format specifier `{s}` in last PR #22, it makes it easier to parse strings, and formatted strings!

author: knst
body:
## Issue being fixed or feature implemented
Currently, there are 2 handlers for governance in Qt app: `updateProposalList` and `updateVotingCapability`.
`updateVotingCapability` is calling for each block; `updateProposalList` is calling once in 10 seconds.
Calling `updateVotingCapability` for each block is very inefficient because during reindex this handler takes uses one full CPU core on my laptop and make Qt app very irresponsible and lagging; it could take up to 10-60 seconds to see an input text in RPC console or react to click.

## What was done?
Call `updateVotingCapability` for each call of `updateProposalList`, no more often.

Minor improvement: use unique_ptr instead shared_ptr in ClientModel: it returns a copy of object anyway currently instead shared_ptr.

## How Has This Been Tested?
This PR makes `updateVotingCapability` disappear from the top of profiler.

This pull request introduces several improvements across documentation, development tooling, automation scripts, and configuration files. The most notable changes include enhanced documentation for git hooks, improved automation logic to skip checks for markdown-only commits, updates to the Makefile for better asset and Docker management, and dependency upgrades for development tools and gems.

**Automation and Developer Tooling Improvements:**

* Added a comprehensive `.githooks/README.md` to document the setup and usage of git hooks, including instructions for skipping hooks and branch-specific exclusions.

The GUI Agent was encountering `Tool "browser_vision_control" not found` errors due to improper operator type handling and unconditional URL content addition in environment events.

**Solution:**
This PR implements a temporary fix with the following changes:

1. **Type-safe operator handling**: Added `instanceof BrowserOperator` check before calling `getMeta()` method to ensure the operator supports browser-specific functionality
2. **Conditional URL content**: Modified the environment event content generation to only include URL information when it's actually available, preventing empty or undefined URL strings from being added to the content array
3. **Import addition**: Added proper import for `BrowserOperator` type to enable runtime type checking

**Key Changes:**
- Modified `GuiAgentPlugin.ts` to check operator type before calling browser-specific methods
- Implemented conditional content array construction based on URL availability
- Enhanced error prevention by avoiding method calls on incompatible operator types

**Impact:**
- Resolves tool not found errors in non-browser operator contexts
- Improves content quality by excluding empty URL information
- Maintains backward compatibility with existing functionality

### Future Plan

**Next Steps: Operator Interface Refactoring**

This current implementation serves as a temporary solution. The long-term plan involves:

1. **Operator Interface Standardization**: Refactor the base `Operator` interface to include standardized methods for observation data retrieval
2. **Unified Observation API**: Design a common interface that all operator types (Browser, Computer, etc.) can implement to provide consistent observation data
3. **Enhanced GUI Agent Integration**: Update GUI Agent to work seamlessly with the new unified observation interface, eliminating the need for type-specific checks
4. **Improved Extensibility**: Enable easier addition of new operator types without requiring GUI Agent modifications

The refactoring will provide a more robust and maintainable architecture for operator-agent communication while preserving all current functionality.

# Description

This PR fixes a bug where the name value was not initialized before making MFA-related API calls. As a result, recoverMfa and requestResetMfa could fail due to missing or incorrect identifiers.

## Reasoning

The name value is required for MFA recovery and reset operations. Without explicitly initializing it from localStorage, these functions could behave unexpectedly or fail entirely if name.value is empty or undefined.

## Changes introduced
Load name from localStorage in:
- recoverMfa
- requestMfaReset

## How to test

1. Simulate an MFA recovery or reset flow without prior setting of name.
2. Confirm that the name is correctly loaded from localStorage.
3. Ensure the API calls succeed with the expected parameters.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The SimpleGo backend was missing the `ConvGeneralDilated` operation, causing failures when running convolution-based models like the [styletransfer example](https://github.com/janpfeifer/styletransfer) with the `simplego` backend. This resulted in a panic:

```
panic: sorry, op "ConvGeneralDilated" not implemented in SimpleGo yet -- reach out to github.com/gomlx/gomlx and open an issue if you need this op, this helps us prioritize the work: not implemented
```

This issue was preventing users from running neural networks with convolution layers on platforms where the XLA backend is not available, limiting GoMLX's portability.

## Solution

This PR implements a complete `ConvGeneralDilated` operation for the SimpleGo backend, addressing [issue #191](https://github.com/gomlx/gomlx/issues/191). The implementation includes:

### Shape Inference
- Added `ConvGeneralDilatedOp` function that validates input parameters and calculates output shapes
- Handles default values for strides, paddings, and dilations when not specified
- Validates channel dimensions, group counts, and spatial dimension compatibility

### Operation Registration
- Implemented `ConvGeneralDilated` function in the SimpleGo backend builder
- Added proper node creation and parameter storage for the computation graph

### Execution Engine
- Full convolution execution logic supporting:
  - Multiple data types: Float32, Float64, and BFloat16
  - Batch and filter grouping for advanced convolution patterns
  - Input and filter dilations for atrous/dilated convolutions
  - Configurable strides and padding
  - Arbitrary spatial dimensions (1D, 2D, 3D, etc.)

### Integration
- Enabled the operation in SimpleGo backend capabilities
- Generated dispatcher mappings for type-safe execution
- Maintains compatibility with existing GoMLX graph API

## Testing

The implementation has been thoroughly tested with:

```go
// Basic 2D convolution
input: [1, 3, 3, 1] -> output: [1, 2, 2, 1] ✓

// Convolution with padding 
input: [1, 3, 3, 1] -> output: [1, 3, 3, 1] (same size) ✓

// Convolution with strides
input: [1, 4, 4, 1] -> output: [1, 2, 2, 1] (downsampled) ✓
```

Mathematical correctness has been validated and existing tests continue to pass without regressions.

## Impact

- ✅ Enables convolution-based models to run on the portable SimpleGo backend
- ✅ Improves GoMLX compatibility across platforms where XLA is unavailable  
- ✅ Maintains performance through optimized iteration patterns and memory locality
- ✅ Follows established codebase patterns and architecture

Models requiring convolution operations can now successfully execute with the SimpleGo backend, significantly expanding GoMLX's usability for deployment scenarios requiring maximum portability.

author: copilot
body:
This PR adds a new **Remote ESP32** component to the Owntracks OSM repository, enabling ESP32 microcontrollers to participate in the existing location sharing ecosystem alongside the Samsung smartwatch app.

## What's Added

The new `Remote_ESP32/` directory contains a complete Arduino-compatible project that allows ESP32 devices to send location data to the same MQTT broker used by the Owntracks OSM smartwatch app.

### Key Features

- **WiFi connectivity** for MQTT communication with Owntracks brokers
- **GPS location tracking** support with optional GPS modules (NEO-6M, NEO-8M)
- **Full Owntracks protocol compatibility** - works seamlessly with existing smartwatch app
- **Battery level monitoring** and reporting
- **Configurable update frequency** (10 seconds to 1 hour)
- **TLS/SSL support** for secure broker connections
- **Comprehensive documentation** with setup guides and troubleshooting

### Project Structure

```
Remote_ESP32/
├── Remote_ESP32.ino          # Main Arduino sketch
├── config.h.example          # Configuration template
├── README.md                 # Complete setup guide
├── platformio.ini            # PlatformIO project config
├── examples/
│   ├── GPS_Enhanced_Remote_ESP32.ino  # GPS-enabled version
│   └── Diagnostic_Test.ino            # Testing utilities
├── PROTOCOL.md               # Owntracks message format docs
├── WIRING.md                 # Hardware connection diagrams
└── libraries.txt             # Required Arduino libraries
```

### Integration Benefits

- **Extends ecosystem**: Add multiple remote tracking devices to your Owntracks setup
- **Cost-effective**: ESP32 boards are inexpensive compared to smartwatches
- **Flexible deployment**: Battery-powered, weatherproof enclosures for vehicles, pets, equipment
- **Unified interface**: All devices appear together in the Owntracks OSM smartwatch app

### Usage Example

After configuration, the ESP32 sends standard Owntracks JSON messages:

```json
{
  "_type": "location",
  "lat": -35.30826,
  "lon": 149.12447,
  "acc": 10,
  "tst": 1693612800,
  "batt": 95,
  "tid": "E1",
  "sat": 8
}
```

These messages are immediately visible on the smartwatch app's map, allowing users to track multiple devices from a single interface.

### Documentation

The component includes comprehensive documentation covering:
- Hardware requirements and wiring diagrams
- Software installation (Arduino IDE and PlatformIO)
- Configuration setup for WiFi and MQTT
- Troubleshooting common issues
- Protocol specifications for developers

This addition transforms the Owntracks OSM project from a single-device solution into a complete IoT location tracking ecosystem while maintaining full backward compatibility with the existing smartwatch application.

body:
## Problem The `ReportContractTests` were failing because the HTML renderer was generating section headers that didn't match the test expectations when converted to lowercase for comparison. Specifically, the tests were looking for German terms like "gültigkeit", "rt60 bericht", and "rt60 je frequenz" but the HTML renderer was using different variations. ## Root Cause The HTML renderer in `AcoustiScanConsolidated/Sources/AcoustiScanConsolidated/ReportHTMLRenderer.swift` was using: - "Gutachterlicher Raumakustik Report" (test expected "rt60 bericht") - "RT60-Frequenzanalyse" (test expected "rt60 je frequenz") - "Validität" (test expected "gültigkeit") When the HTML content is processed by tests using regex to strip HTML tags and converted to lowercase, these mismatches caused test failures. ## Solution Updated the section headers in the HTML renderer to use the exact German terms expected by the tests: ```swift // Before

Gutachterlicher Raumakustik Report

RT60-Frequenzanalyse

Validität

// After

RT60 Bericht

RT60 je Frequenz

Gültigkeit

``` ## Impact - ✅ All 21 tests now pass in `AcoustiScanConsolidated` module - ✅ All 4 tests continue to pass in `Export` module - ✅ Ensures PDF and HTML outputs contain all required tokens: - Frequency labels (125, 1000, 4000, etc.) - DIN target values (0.65, 0.55, 0.15, 0.12, etc.) - Core metadata tokens ("rt60 bericht", "metadaten", "gerät", etc.) - Missing values properly shown as "-" ## Changes Made - **1 file changed**: `AcoustiScanConsolidated/Sources/AcoustiScanConsolidated/ReportHTMLRenderer.swift` - **3 lines modified**: Updated section headers only - **Minimal impact**: No functional changes to PDF generation or data processing logic This fix ensures the HTML renderer produces content that matches the contract test expectations while maintaining full compatibility with existing PDF generation functionality. --- 💡 You can make Copilot smarter by setting up custom instructions, customizing its development environment and configuring Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. author: trobacker
body:
This PR is related to #464 and adds the scoring results from at least 90 days past today's date, `2025-09-02`. 

We add scores titled by their submission deadline date (a Wednesday - e.g. `2025-05-28`) into the directory `./auxiliary-data/scores`.

One can read scores for a particular nowcast submission date, for example:
`df_scores <- arrow::read_parquet("./auxiliary-data/scores/2025-05-28.parquet")`

then aggregate by team the mean energy and mean brier scores:
`df_scores |> group_by(team) |> summarize(mean_energy = mean(energy, na.rm = T), mean_brier = mean(brier, na.rm = T))`

Users can now perform EDA on scores which are available at each time point (day) and location. 

This PR manually adds the scores and we will want to consider automating the scoring process in the near future.

## Summary
Implements Track B, B2 from the billing portal migration plan - Payment Method Procedures for the customer billing portal.

This PR adds two new TRPC procedures to enable payment method management in the self-hosted billing portal:
- `createAddPaymentMethodSession` - Creates a Stripe Checkout session in setup mode for adding payment methods
- `setDefaultPaymentMethod` - Updates the default payment method in both Stripe and database

- Both procedures use `customerProtectedProcedure` for proper authentication
- Customer ownership validation ensures users can only manage their own payment methods
- Integration with Stripe API for payment method operations
- Proper error handling with descriptive TRPC errors
- The `removePaymentMethod` procedure was intentionally not included as delete flows are not ready to be reasoned about

author: blblack
body:
Previously we had a single definition of std.c.cmsghdr for all libc-linking platforms which aliased from the Solaris definition, a superfluous matching one in std.os.dragonfly, and no others.

The existing definition from std.c didn't actually work for Linux, as Linux's "len" field is usize in the kernel's definition.

Emscripten follows the Linux model of course (but uses the binary-compatible musl definition, which has an endian-sensitive padding scheme to make the len type "socklen_t" even though the kernel uses a usize, which is fair).

This unifies and documents all the known *nix-ish cases (I'm not sure if wasi or windows really has cmsghdr support? Could be added later, void for now), such that c.cmsghdr and posix.system.cmsghdr should work correctly for all the known cases here, libc or otherwise.

body:
https://github.com/ydb-platform/nbs/issues/3783

Currently NBS disk are usually mounted locally. However for the disks which are actually running in different cell it is better for the proxy host to the mount them remotely and let HIVE in different cell to decide where to run the tablet. But this could introduce addional network hop. In order to avoid this, MountVolume response should include new field, HostName which is a fqdn of the host where tablet is currently running. This information will be used to reconnect to the host of tablet, to reduce the number of network hops.

body:
This pull request introduces comprehensive enhancements to the SQS worker example and the AWS IAM module documentation. It adds two new SQS worker deployment patterns (direct access and AssumeRole), improves the worker code to support AssumeRole authentication, and significantly expands the IAM README with detailed usage, configuration, and permissions guidance.

**SQS Worker Example Enhancements:**

* Added a new example for direct access: creates an IAM user with SQS permissions and generates access keys automatically for the worker (`sqs-worker-direct-access.yaml`).
* Added a new example for AssumeRole: creates a minimal IAM user that can assume a service role with SQS permissions, enabling temporary, rotated credentials for the worker (`sqs-worker-assume-role.yaml`).
* Updated the main example to reference and explain these enhanced patterns, guiding users toward best practices for production deployments (`sqs-worker.yaml`).

**Worker Application Improvements:**

* Updated `worker.ts` to detect and use AssumeRole credentials if relevant environment variables are set, falling back to direct credentials otherwise. This enables seamless switching between authentication patterns without code changes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9a2687be644b37c6ae9f47f3de82eeeba11f735e22e8a504351594b84c9a78ffR2-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-9a2687be644b37c6ae9f47f3de82eeeba11f735e22e8a504351594b84c9a78ffR25-R59)
* Added dependencies for STS and credential providers to support AssumeRole in the Node.js worker (`package.json`).

**AWS IAM Module Documentation Upgrades:**

* Expanded the `aws-iam` README to cover users, roles, and policies, including new sections for entity features, configuration parameters, and usage examples for both direct access and AssumeRole patterns. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c3ac7eea430646c76e3188a320d2fb0274032179ab860f1cd96d466480805b97L1-R115) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c3ac7eea430646c76e3188a320d2fb0274032179ab860f1cd96d466480805b97L83-R283)
* Added detailed documentation for IAM user and role management, including required permissions for each entity type and custom actions for user management. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c3ac7eea430646c76e3188a320d2fb0274032179ab860f1cd96d466480805b97R325) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c3ac7eea430646c76e3188a320d2fb0274032179ab860f1cd96d466480805b97R351-R400)

These changes provide robust, production-ready SQS worker deployment patterns and make the IAM module much easier to use and understand for both direct credential and AssumeRole scenarios.

- Future enhancement timeline with versioned feature additions
- Clear progression from basic functionality (v1.1 search) to advanced features (v2.0 cloud sync)

The original plan.md provided excellent technical specifications but lacked practical guidance for contributors. These additions transform the document from a feature specification into a comprehensive project guide that enables:

In Conv3d, dimension of kernel sizes should be specified D, H, W order.

https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Conv3d.html

However, current code of padding handle as if it were ordered in H, W, D order.

This can harm architecture modification of anisotropic kernel size like (3, 1, 1) or (1, 3, 3).

This PR will fix this bug.

PR for upstream: https://github.com/ZFTurbo/timm_3d/pull/8

author: copilot
body:
This PR fixes two critical issues preventing the Matrix plugin from functioning correctly:

## Issue 1: TypeError: this.client?.getRoom is not a function

The code was calling `this.client.getRoom(roomId)` throughout the codebase, but this method doesn't exist in matrix-bot-sdk v0.7.1. This was causing runtime errors whenever the bot tried to process room events or get room information.

**Root cause:** The matrix-bot-sdk doesn't provide a `getRoom()` method. The available methods are more granular, like `getRoomState()`, `getRoomMembers()`, etc.

**Solution:** 
- Created a `getRoomInfo()` helper method that aggregates room information using valid SDK methods
- Replaced all 11 instances of `getRoom()` calls across service, providers, and actions
- Added a custom `MatrixRoom` interface to replace the missing Room type from the SDK

## Issue 2: No encryption provider set up

The plugin wasn't configured with encryption support as mentioned in the Matrix bot SDK documentation, preventing it from working with encrypted rooms.

**Solution:**
- Added `RustSdkCryptoStorageProvider` configuration when `MATRIX_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED=true`
- Added proper encryption initialization following the Matrix bot SDK tutorial
- Included graceful fallback when encryption setup fails

## Technical Details

The `getRoomInfo()` helper method constructs room information by:
- Using `getRoomState()` to extract room name, topic, avatar, and encryption status
- Using `getRoomMembers()` to get member count and detect direct message rooms
- Using `getAccountData('m.direct')` to properly identify DM rooms
- Providing fallback values when data isn't available

## Files Changed
- `src/service.ts`: Added helper methods and encryption setup
- `src/types.ts`: Added `MatrixRoom` interface, removed invalid Room import
- `src/providers/roomState.ts`: Updated to use new helper method
- `src/actions/listRooms.ts`: Updated to use new helper method  
- `src/actions/leaveRoom.ts`: Updated to use new helper method

## Testing
- ✅ All existing tests continue to pass
- ✅ Build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Code formatting fixed with prettier
- ✅ No remaining `getRoom()` method calls found

This is a surgical fix that maintains full backward compatibility while resolving the core functionality issues.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The current map exploration system stores user exploration data in the MapTile's `exploredBy` field as an array of explorer names. This approach becomes inefficient for large maps because:

- Checking if a colony has explored a tile requires scanning through the `exploredBy` array
- MapTile documents become bloated with user-specific exploration data
- Querying for colony-specific exploration requires array operations that don't scale well

## Solution

Implemented a new `UserMapTile` schema that separates user-specific exploration tracking from the authoritative map data, providing efficient O(1) lookups while maintaining data integrity.

### Key Changes

**New UserMapTile Schema:**
- Tracks which colonies have explored which tiles using indexed references
- Unique constraint on `(serverTile, colonyId)` prevents duplicate records
- Stores colony-specific exploration metadata (exploredAt, discoveredLoot, etc.)

**Updated Exploration System:**
- `canTileBeExplored()` now uses UserMapTile for adjacent tile checks
- `startExploration()` creates UserMapTile records instead of updating exploredBy arrays  
- `getMapGridForColony()` uses UserMapTile for efficient fog of war determination
- Colony creation automatically creates initial UserMapTile for homestead location
- Exploration completion ensures UserMapTile records are created

**Performance Improvements:**
- Colony-specific exploration queries now use indexed lookups instead of array scans
- MapTile documents remain focused on authoritative tile content (terrain, loot, threats)
- Fog of war system scales efficiently with large maps and many colonies

**Clean Architecture:**
- Completely removed `MapTile.exploredBy` field from schema and interface
- Eliminated all code that populated or referenced exploredBy arrays
- Updated client-side types to remove exploredBy field
- Cleaned up API responses to not include deprecated fields
- Updated all tests to work without exploredBy references

### Architecture

```
MapTile (authoritative)          UserMapTile (per-colony tracking)
├── serverId, x, y              ├── serverTile (ref to MapTile)  
├── terrain, loot, threats      ├── colonyId
└── colony (first explorer)     └── exploredAt
```

**MapTile** remains the single source of truth for tile content - terrain types, loot spawns, threats, and events. When a user explores a tile, we first check if a MapTile exists (created by another player). If it exists, we use its authoritative data; if not, we create a new one.

**UserMapTile** efficiently tracks which colonies have explored which tiles using indexed foreign key relationships, enabling fast O(1) lookups for fog of war and exploration validation.

### Testing

Added comprehensive tests for:
- UserMapTile model constraints and relationships
- Map utility functions (createUserMapTile, hasColonyExploredTile)
- Integration with exploration workflow
- Unique constraint enforcement

This change enables the game to scale to much larger maps with many active colonies while maintaining fast response times for exploration and map rendering.

body:
## 연관된 이슈

- close #554 

## 작업 내용

**파일 로그를 json 포맷으로 변경**
기존 로그는 다음과 같이 로그를 별도로 파싱해야하는 번거로움이 존재했습니다.
```
parse '* * * * traceId="*" *' as date, time, level, class, traceId, message
| filter level in ["ERROR"]
...
```
이러한 번거로움을 없애고 로그 분석을 쉽게하기 위해 파일 로그를 다음과 같이 json 포맷으로 encoding하도록 변경했습니다.

```
// 로그
{"@timestamp":"2025-09-04T17:30:04.35749+09:00","level":"INFO","logger":"org.springframework.orm.jpa.LocalContainerEntityManagerFactoryBean","msg":"Closing JPA EntityManagerFactory for persistence unit 'default'"}
```

```
// 별도의 파싱이 필요 없음.
filter level in ["ERROR"]
...
```

---

**로그 파일 rolling**

기존에는 모든 로그가 하나의 로그 파일에 저장되어 이전 히스토리를 쉽게 찾아보기 힘들다는 단점이 존재했습니다.
따라서 logback을 활용해 일자별로 파일을 분할 관리할 수 있도록 수정했습니다.

또한 어느정도 기한이 지난 로그들은 불필요하다고 생각해 로그 파일의 보관 기간을 지정해주었습니다.
개발 : 7일
운영 : 30일
기간은 넉넉 잡아 산정했고, 프로젝트 진행하며 상황에 맞게 변경할 수 있습니다.

---

**로그 레벨 변경**
- 사용자의 잘못된 요청으로 인한 예측 가능한 예외: WARN → INFO
WARN 레벨은 보안 관련 예외나 잠재적 위험 요소를 모니터링하는 용도로 사용하고,
사용자의 일반적인 입력/비즈니스 검증 예외는 비교적 위험도가 낮기 때문에 INFO 레벨로 남기는 것이 적절하다고 판단했습니다.

- HTTP 요청 및 응답 로그: INFO → TRACE
INFO 레벨은 비즈니스적으로 의미 있는 이벤트 기록 용도이고,
INFO 레벨에서의 HTTP 요청/응답 로그는 노이즈로 작용한다고 판단했습니다.
따라서 TRACE 레벨로 변경했습니다.

body: ## Type of Change - [ ] Bugfix - [ ] New feature - [x] Enhancement - [ ] Refactoring - [ ] Dependency updates - [ ] Documentation - [ ] CI/CD ## Description This PR refactors the gRPC header handling for the Unified Connector Service (UCS) by introducing a dedicated header type, `GrpcHeadersUcs`. This change enhances the specificity and robustness of header management for UCS interactions. Key changes include: - **New `GrpcHeadersUcs` Struct**: A new struct, `GrpcHeadersUcs`, has been introduced in `crates/external_services/src/grpc_client.rs`. It specifically caters to UCS needs and includes `tenant_id`, `lineage_ids`, and `external_vault_proxy_metadata` fields, utilizing the `TypedBuilder` pattern for instantiation. - **Enhanced UCS Header Construction**: The `build_unified_connector_service_grpc_headers` function in `crates/external_services/src/grpc_client/unified_connector_service.rs` now accepts `GrpcHeadersUcs`. It includes new logic to properly URL-encode and inject `lineage_ids` into the gRPC metadata, using a newly added constant `UCS_LINEAGE_IDS`. - **Updated UCS Client Methods**: All relevant methods in `UnifiedConnectorServiceClient` have been updated to accept `GrpcHeadersUcs` instead of the generic `GrpcHeaders`. - **Router Flow Updates**: Calls within various payment flows (`authorize_flow.rs`, `external_proxy_flow.rs`, `psync_flow.rs`, `setup_mandate_flow.rs`) and the core UCS module (`unified_connector_service.rs`) have been updated to use the new `state.get_grpc_headers_ucs()` method and adapt to the `GrpcHeadersUcs` builder pattern. ### Additional Changes - [ ] This PR modifies the API contract - [ ] This PR modifies the database schema - [ ] This PR modifies application configuration/environment variables ## Motivation and Context The primary motivation for this change is to create a clear separation between general gRPC headers and those specifically required by the Unified Connector Service. The previous implementation used a generic `GrpcHeaders` struct for UCS, which was not ideal as UCS has specific requirements, notably for `lineage_ids`. This refactoring allows for: - **Improved Clarity and Maintainability**: By having a dedicated struct for UCS headers, the code becomes easier to understand and maintain. - **Type Safety**: Ensures that UCS-specific header fields like `lineage_ids` are correctly handled where needed. - **Enhanced Functionality**: Facilitates the proper encoding and inclusion of `lineage_ids` in gRPC metadata, which is crucial for UCS operations. ## How did you test it? This change was primarily a refactoring effort. The existing test suite should cover the functionality, as the external behavior of UCS calls remains the same. The changes were verified by: - Ensuring the code compiles without errors. - Reviewing the modified logic for header construction and injection to confirm correctness. lineage_merchant_id is being populated in UCS events.

# Description


Removed duplicate distributionKeeper.EXPECT().FundCommunityPool(...).Return(nil).AnyTimes() in setupGovKeeper, keeping only the balance-aware DoAndReturn from trackMockBalances.

author: copilot
body:
This PR resolves critical issues in the authentication token refresh flow that were preventing proper automatic token renewal and causing authentication failures.

## Issues Fixed

### 1. Frontend Token Storage Inconsistency
The application had inconsistent token storage across components:
- `useAuth.js` was checking `sessionStorage.getItem("accessToken")`
- `axios.js` was using `localStorage.getItem("token")`
- `Login.jsx` was storing `localStorage.setItem("token", accessToken)`

This mismatch caused authentication state to be out of sync between components.

### 2. Malformed Refresh Token API Call
The axios interceptor had an incorrect refresh token API call:

```javascript
// Before (incorrect)
const res = await axios.post(
  "http://localhost:3000/user/refresh-token",
  {
    withCredentials: true,  // ❌ Should be in config, not body
  }
);

// After (correct)
const res = await axios.post(
  "http://localhost:3000/user/refresh-token",
  {}, // Empty body since refresh token is sent via cookies
  {
    withCredentials: true, // ✅ Correct placement in config
  }
);
```

### 3. Incorrect Response Data Access
The frontend was trying to access `res.data.accessToken` directly, but the backend API response structure is nested: `res.data.data.accessToken`.

### 4. Cookie Security and Configuration Issues
- Cookies were always set with `secure: false`, inappropriate for production
- No differentiation between access token and refresh token expiry times
- Missing proper SameSite configuration for CSRF protection

### 5. Poor Error Handling
- Generic JWT error messages made debugging difficult
- No cleanup of invalid refresh tokens from the database
- Missing specific error types for different JWT validation failures

## Changes Made

### Frontend Improvements
- **Standardized token storage** to use `localStorage.getItem("token")` consistently
- **Fixed axios refresh call** configuration and response data access
- **Enhanced error handling** with proper cleanup of both token and user data on refresh failure

### Backend Improvements
- **Enhanced cookie security** with environment-aware settings:
  ```javascript
  {
    secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === "production",
    sameSite: process.env.NODE_ENV === "production" ? "none" : "strict",
    maxAge: 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000, // 7 days for refresh token
  }
  ```
- **Implemented differentiated token expiry**:
  - Access tokens: 15 minutes
  - Refresh tokens: 7 days
- **Improved JWT error handling** with specific error types:
  - `TokenExpiredError`: "Access token has expired. Please refresh your token."
  - `JsonWebTokenError`: "Invalid access token format."
  - `NotBeforeError`: "Token not active yet."
- **Enhanced refresh token validation** with database cleanup of invalid tokens
- **Fixed logout functionality** to properly remove refresh tokens from database using `$unset`

## Security Enhancements
- HTTP-only cookies prevent XSS attacks on refresh tokens
- Secure cookies in production (HTTPS-only)
- SameSite protection against CSRF attacks
- Short access token lifespan reduces impact of token theft
- Refresh token rotation on each refresh
- Automatic cleanup of invalid tokens from database

## Testing
- All syntax checks pass
- Frontend builds successfully without errors
- Backend components validated
- Verification script confirms all fixes are properly applied

The token refresh flow now works reliably with proper automatic retry of failed requests and comprehensive error handling.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The bandgap crystal generation scripts (`generate_bandgap_crystals.py` and `generate_bandgap_range.py`) were failing with the following error:

```
AssertionError: Only one of pretrained_name or model_path can be provided.
```

This occurred when running commands like:
```bash
python generate_bandgap_crystals.py --band_gap 1.0 --output_dir results_bg_1.0 --batch_size 16
```

## Root Cause

The issue was caused by improper shell argument parsing when using `os.system()` to execute the mattergen generate command. The scripts constructed commands with dictionary arguments containing curly braces:

```bash
python -m mattergen.scripts.generate results_bg_1.0 --pretrained-name=dft_band_gap --properties_to_condition_on={'dft_band_gap': 1.0}
```

When passed to `os.system()`, bash interpreted the unquoted curly braces and incorrectly split the argument:
- `--properties_to_condition_on={dft_band_gap:` (first part)  
- `1.0}` (second part)

The second part (`1.0}`) was then interpreted by `fire.Fire()` as a positional argument for `model_path`, causing both `pretrained_name` and `model_path` to be set simultaneously, which violates the assertion in `mattergen/scripts/generate.py`.

## Solution

Replaced `os.system()` with `subprocess.run()` using `shell=False` to pass arguments directly without shell interpretation:

```python
# Before (broken)
cmd = " ".join(cmd_parts)
exit_code = os.system(cmd)

# After (fixed)  
cmd = " ".join(cmd_parts)  # Still display the command for users
result = subprocess.run(cmd_parts, shell=False)  # Execute safely
exit_code = result.returncode
```

This ensures that dictionary arguments are preserved as single, properly formatted strings and prevents bash from expanding curly braces incorrectly.

## Files Changed

- `generate_bandgap_crystals.py`: Fixed shell argument parsing and added subprocess import
- `generate_bandgap_range.py`: Applied the same fix to prevent identical issues

## Testing

Verified the fix by:
1. Confirming the old method incorrectly splits `--properties_to_condition_on={'dft_band_gap': 1.0}` into multiple arguments
2. Validating the new method preserves arguments correctly as single strings
3. Testing that the `fire.Fire()` assertions now pass with properly formatted arguments

This resolves the `AssertionError` and allows the bandgap generation scripts to execute successfully.

3. packages/smart-accounts/src/light-account/accounts/multi-owner-account.test.ts: run suite sequentially and added retries to the longest test.

**Impact:**

1. Reduces cross-test interference and thread contention.
2. Adds resilience to transient network hiccups.

#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
In 179551a, warnings are returned for unrecognized CRD formats, however int32, int64, float, and double were not being recognized, conflicting with existing behavior. Later in 4e200ca, warnings were restricted to only type=string.

This commit adds validation to types integer and number and returns warnings when formats are not supported.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Fixes #133880

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

author: copilot
body:
This PR addresses critical security vulnerabilities and implements comprehensive security enhancements for the Solana Forensics application following a thorough security audit.

## 🔒 Critical Security Issues Fixed

### Hard-coded Admin Credentials
The application had hard-coded admin wallet addresses in both `middleware.ts` and `app/login/page.tsx`. This created a security risk where admin access logic was exposed and immutable:

```typescript
// Before (INSECURE)
const isAdmin = walletAddress === "AuwUfiwsXA6VibDjR579HWLhDUUoa5s6T7i7KPyLUa9F"

// After (SECURE)
const adminWalletAddress = process.env.ADMIN_WALLET_ADDRESS
const isAdmin = adminWalletAddress && walletAddress === adminWalletAddress
```

### Next.js Security Vulnerabilities
Updated Next.js from 15.2.4 to 15.5.2 to resolve three moderate-severity CVEs:
- **GHSA-xv57-4mr9-wg8v**: Content Injection Vulnerability in Image Optimization
- **GHSA-4342-x723-ch2f**: SSRF via Improper Middleware Redirect Handling  
- **GHSA-g5qg-72qw-gw5v**: Cache Key Confusion for Image Optimization API Routes

### API Security Hardening
API endpoints were vulnerable to injection attacks and information disclosure:

```typescript
// Added input validation for Solana addresses
if (!/^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$/.test(address)) {
  return NextResponse.json({ error: "Invalid address format" }, { status: 400 })
}

// Sanitized error responses to prevent information leakage
if (status === 401 || status === 403) {
  return { error: "API authentication failed" }
}
```

## 🛡️ Security Enhancements Implemented

### Security Headers and CSP
Added comprehensive HTTP security headers in `next.config.mjs`:
- Content Security Policy to prevent XSS attacks
- X-Frame-Options to prevent clickjacking
- X-Content-Type-Options to prevent MIME sniffing
- X-XSS-Protection for legacy browser support

### Rate Limiting and Request Validation
Implemented security middleware (`lib/api-security.ts`) with:
- IP-based rate limiting (60 requests/minute)
- Request validation and suspicious pattern detection
- Security event logging for monitoring

### Input Validation Utilities
Created `lib/security.ts` with utilities for:
- Solana address format validation
- Input sanitization to prevent injection attacks
- Security event logging for audit trails

## 🔧 Security Tools and Automation

### Automated Security Scanner
Added `scripts/security-check.js` that detects:
- Hardcoded secrets in source code
- Missing security configurations
- Environment file exposure risks
- API input validation coverage

### Security-focused ESLint Rules
Configured `.eslintrc.json` with security-specific rules:
- Detection of dangerous React patterns (`react/no-danger`)
- Security plugin rules for common vulnerabilities
- TypeScript strict mode enforcement

## 📚 Documentation and Best Practices

### Security Analysis Report
Created `SECURITY_ANALYSIS.md` with:
- Detailed vulnerability assessment findings
- Risk classifications and impact analysis
- Compliance considerations for financial applications

### Security Best Practices Guide  
Added `SECURITY_GUIDE.md` covering:
- Environment variable security
- Ongoing security maintenance tasks
- Incident response procedures
- CI/CD security integration recommendations

### Environment Configuration Template
Provided `.env.example` with:
- All required environment variables documented
- Security-focused configuration guidance
- Clear separation of public vs private variables

## 🏃‍♂️ How to Use

Run the security audit tools:
```bash
npm run security:audit  # Comprehensive security analysis
npm audit              # Check for vulnerable dependencies
```

Configure environment variables:
```bash
cp .env.example .env.local
# Edit .env.local with your actual credentials
```

## 🎯 Security Impact

**Before**: Multiple critical vulnerabilities (HIGH RISK)
- Hard-coded credentials
- Known CVEs in dependencies  
- Missing input validation
- Information disclosure in errors
- No security headers

**After**: Significantly improved security posture (MEDIUM RISK)
- Environment-based configuration
- Updated secure dependencies
- Comprehensive input validation
- Sanitized error handling
- Multi-layer security headers

This PR transforms the application from a high-risk security state to a well-protected system following modern web application security best practices and OWASP guidelines.

body:
This pull request adds a new graph visualization feature to the web crawler, allowing users to generate visual network graphs of page relationships. The feature is integrated into the CLI, documented in the `README.md`, and implemented in a new file, `graph_visualizer.go`. Additional dependencies for image and font rendering are also introduced.

**Graph Visualization Feature:**

* Added a new `graph_visualizer.go` module implementing a graph visualization engine using the `github.com/fogleman/gg` library. It generates PNG images showing internal and external page relationships with color-coded nodes, scalable sizing, smart labeling, and a built-in legend.
* Updated CLI usage to support an optional `--graph` flag, which triggers graph generation after crawling. The flag is documented in usage messages and the README examples. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2873f79a86c0d8b3335cd7731b0ecf7dd4301eb19a82ef7a1cba7589b5252261L94-R106) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2873f79a86c0d8b3335cd7731b0ecf7dd4301eb19a82ef7a1cba7589b5252261R176-R186) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2873f79a86c0d8b3335cd7731b0ecf7dd4301eb19a82ef7a1cba7589b5252261R217-R226) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L47-R57) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R66) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R85-R90) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L91-R105)

**Documentation Updates:**

* Expanded the `README.md` to describe the graph visualization feature, including usage instructions, sample output, and a detailed explanation of graph elements and features. body: ## What? Part of #71517 Fixes https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/71552 Tests out an idea of making all unsynced patterns `contentOnly` when inserted. At the moment this is missing some niceties, like being able to 'unlock' the pattern to edit it fully. The PR is just to see how it feels, but I'd welcome anyone to add commits with additional features. ## How? this PR is based on [Refactor: Content only template locking block editing modes to reducer](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/67606#top), which makes it much easier to implement. body:
## Summary

Fix critical segmentation fault in the `CircularBPFixture/CorrelationCancellationOverhead` benchmark that was causing the engines_benchmarks executable to crash after completion.

## Root Cause Analysis

The benchmark was calling `.unwrap()` on a `Result<T,E>` without first checking if the result was valid:

```cpp
// UNSAFE - Line 160
auto no_cancel_engine_result = create_circular_bp_engine(no_cancel_config);
auto no_cancel_engine = std::move(no_cancel_engine_result).unwrap(); // ⚠️ No error check
```

When `create_circular_bp_engine()` returned an error, calling `.unwrap()` on the failed Result caused undefined behavior, leading to segmentation fault after the benchmark completed.

## Fix Applied

Added proper `Result<T,E>` error handling following the project's established patterns:

```cpp
// SAFE - After fix
auto no_cancel_engine_result = create_circular_bp_engine(no_cancel_config);
if (no_cancel_engine_result.is_err()) {
    state.SkipWithError("Failed to create CircularBP engine without correlation cancellation");
    return;
}
auto no_cancel_engine = std::move(no_cancel_engine_result).unwrap();
```

Also improved error handling consistency in the `SetUp()` method.

## Testing Results

✅ **Before Fix**: Segmentation fault after benchmark completion
```
CircularBPFixture/CorrelationCancellationOverhead     150454 ns       150129 ns         4506
[1]    81716 segmentation fault  ./engines_benchmarks
```

✅ **After Fix**: Benchmark runs successfully without crashes
- Both engines execute properly (showing alternating correlation cancellation behavior)
- Graceful error handling if engine creation fails
- All pre-commit checks pass (formatting, static analysis, build verification)

## Impact

This fix ensures:
- ✅ No more segmentation faults in CircularBP benchmarks
- ✅ Proper adherence to project's `Result<T,E>` error handling patterns
- ✅ Graceful benchmark failure handling with `state.SkipWithError()`
- ✅ Continued functionality for performance regression testing

## Files Modified

- `engines/benchmarks/circular_bp_benchmarks.cpp` - Added proper Result error checking

author: miguel-ls
body:
This commit provides a definitive fix for a bug where client-side `fetch` calls to the external `api.apis.net.pe` were failing due to browser CORS restrictions.

A new server-side proxy endpoint, `proxy_sunat`, has been created in `clientes_controller.php`. This endpoint receives the document type and number from the client, makes a secure server-to-server call to the external API, and relays the JSON response back to the client.

The JavaScript files (`cliente_form.js` and `matricula_form.js`) have been updated to call this new internal proxy endpoint instead of the external API directly.

This architecture bypasses browser security restrictions and provides a robust, reliable way to fetch data from the external service.

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR pins [pytest](https://pypi.org/project/pytest) to the latest release **8.4.2**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 8.4.1
   ```
   =========================

Bug fixes
---------

- `13461 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13461>`_: Corrected ``_pytest.terminal.TerminalReporter.isatty`` to support
  being called as a method. Before it was just a boolean which could
  break correct code when using ``-o log_cli=true``).


- `13477 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13477>`_: Reintroduced :class:`pytest.PytestReturnNotNoneWarning` which was removed by accident in pytest `8.4`.

  This warning is raised when a test functions returns a value other than ``None``, which is often a mistake made by beginners.

  See :ref:`return-not-none` for more information.


- `13497 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13497>`_: Fixed compatibility with ``Twisted 25+``.



Improved documentation
----------------------

- `13492 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13492>`_: Fixed outdated warning about ``faulthandler`` not working on Windows.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 8.4.0
   ```
   =========================

Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes
---------------------------------------------------

- `11372 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11372>`_: Async tests will now fail, instead of warning+skipping, if you don't have any suitable plugin installed.


- `12346 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12346>`_: Tests will now fail, instead of raising a warning, if they return any value other than None.


- `12874 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12874>`_: We dropped support for Python 3.8 following its end of life (2024-10-07).


- `12960 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12960>`_: Test functions containing a yield now cause an explicit error. They have not been run since pytest 4.0, and were previously marked as an expected failure and deprecation warning.

  See :ref:`the docs <yield tests deprecated>` for more information.



Deprecations (removal in next major release)
--------------------------------------------

- `10839 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10839>`_: Requesting an asynchronous fixture without a `pytest_fixture_setup` hook that resolves it will now give a DeprecationWarning. This most commonly happens if a sync test requests an async fixture. This should have no effect on a majority of users with async tests or fixtures using async pytest plugins, but may affect non-standard hook setups or ``autouse=True``. For guidance on how to work around this warning see :ref:`sync-test-async-fixture`.



New features
------------

- `11538 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11538>`_: Added :class:`pytest.RaisesGroup` as an equivalent to :func:`pytest.raises` for expecting :exc:`ExceptionGroup`. Also adds :class:`pytest.RaisesExc` which is now the logic behind :func:`pytest.raises` and used as parameter to :class:`pytest.RaisesGroup`. ``RaisesGroup`` includes the ability to specify multiple different expected exceptions, the structure of nested exception groups, and flags for emulating :ref:`except* <except_star>`. See :ref:`assert-matching-exception-groups` and docstrings for more information.


- `12081 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12081>`_: Added :fixture:`capteesys` to capture AND pass output to next handler set by ``--capture=``.


- `12504 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12504>`_: :func:`pytest.mark.xfail` now accepts :class:`pytest.RaisesGroup` for the ``raises`` parameter when you expect an exception group. You can also pass a :class:`pytest.RaisesExc` if you e.g. want to make use of the ``check`` parameter.


- `12713 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12713>`_: New `--force-short-summary` option to force condensed summary output regardless of verbosity level.

  This lets users still see condensed summary output of failures for quick reference in log files from job outputs, being especially useful if non-condensed output is very verbose.


- `12749 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12749>`_: pytest traditionally collects classes/functions in the test module namespace even if they are imported from another file.

  For example:

  .. code-block:: python

       contents of src/domain.py
      class Testament: ...


       contents of tests/test_testament.py
      from domain import Testament


      def test_testament(): ...

  In this scenario with the default options, pytest will collect the class `Testament` from `tests/test_testament.py` because it starts with `Test`, even though in this case it is a production class being imported in the test module namespace.

  This behavior can now be prevented by setting the new :confval:`collect_imported_tests` configuration option to ``false``, which will make pytest collect classes/functions from test files **only** if they are defined in that file.

  -- by :user:`FreerGit`


- `12765 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12765>`_: Thresholds to trigger snippet truncation can now be set with :confval:`truncation_limit_lines` and :confval:`truncation_limit_chars`.

  See :ref:`truncation-params` for more information.


- `13125 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13125>`_: :confval:`console_output_style` now supports ``times`` to show execution time of each test.


- `13192 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13192>`_: :func:`pytest.raises` will now raise a warning when passing an empty string to ``match``, as this will match against any value. Use ``match="^$"`` if you want to check that an exception has no message.


- `13192 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13192>`_: :func:`pytest.raises` will now print a helpful string diff if matching fails and the match parameter has ``^`` and ``$`` and is otherwise escaped.


- `13192 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13192>`_: You can now pass :func:`with pytest.raises(check=fn): <pytest.raises>`, where ``fn`` is a function which takes a raised exception and returns a boolean. The ``raises`` fails if no exception was raised (as usual), passes if an exception is raised and ``fn`` returns ``True`` (as well as ``match`` and the type matching, if specified, which are checked before), and propagates the exception if ``fn`` returns ``False`` (which likely also fails the test).


- `13228 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13228>`_: :ref:`hidden-param` can now be used in ``id`` of :func:`pytest.param` or in
  ``ids`` of :py:func:`Metafunc.parametrize <pytest.Metafunc.parametrize>`.
  It hides the parameter set from the test name.


- `13253 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13253>`_: New flag: :ref:`--disable-plugin-autoload <disable_plugin_autoload>` which works as an alternative to :envvar:`PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD` when setting environment variables is inconvenient; and allows setting it in config files with :confval:`addopts`.



Improvements in existing functionality
--------------------------------------

- `10224 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10224>`_: pytest's ``short`` and ``long`` traceback styles (:ref:`how-to-modifying-python-tb-printing`)
  now have partial :pep:`657` support and will show specific code segments in the
  traceback.

  .. code-block:: pytest

      ================================= FAILURES =================================
      _______________________ test_gets_correct_tracebacks _______________________

      test_tracebacks.py:12: in test_gets_correct_tracebacks
          assert manhattan_distance(p1, p2) == 1
                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
      test_tracebacks.py:6: in manhattan_distance
          return abs(point_1.x - point_2.x) + abs(point_1.y - point_2.y)

## Summary
This feature branch implements the complete SC2 Pattern Learning System with major reliability improvements, clean logging, and robust game state detection.

## Major Features Added
🧠 **SC2 Pattern Learning System**

- AI-powered replay analysis and pattern extraction
- Dual storage: database + JSON file system for patterns/comments

- Automatic connection reset after 5 consecutive failures
- Intelligent URL fallback (localhost → 127.0.0.1)

- Fresh session usage after successful resets

📊 **Clean Log Output System**
- Smart indicator spacing with custom `MarkingStreamHandler`
- Visual indicators (., o, +, x, ?, e) with proper separation from log messages
- Eliminated repetitive DEBUG spam and improved readability

- Fixed `isReplay` handling for proper live game vs replay detection
- Refined MATCH_STARTED/REPLAY_ENDED state transitions
- Proper game ending detection for pattern learning triggers
- Null checks and timeout handling for API stability

⚡ **Performance & Reliability**
- Conditional spacy imports to prevent heavy ML library loading
- Fixed import errors and startup crashes
- Graceful shutdown with Ctrl+C signal handling
- Enhanced error recovery and connection resilience

- ✅ All visual indicators properly spaced

The application likely exits due to the connection failure check in `src/main.ts` before the 10-minute timeout.

**Changes:**
- MODIFY: src/main.ts
- DELETE: ormconfig.ts

author: ikey168
body:
## ✨ AI-Powered Note Summarization Plugin Implementation

This PR implements Issue #27 by introducing an AI-powered note summarization plugin for Modulo.

### 🧠 Features
- **AI Summarization Plugin**: Backend plugin for generating concise summaries of notes using AI models
- **REST API**: Endpoints for summarizing notes, retrieving summaries, and managing summary settings
- **Frontend Components**:
  - SummaryPanel: Displays full AI-generated summary for a note
  - QuickSummary: Inline summary preview for note lists or headers
  - SummaryButton: Toolbar button to trigger or refresh summaries
- **Plugin Architecture**: Follows established plugin system patterns
- **Responsive UI**: Modern, mobile-friendly summary panels and controls

### 🔗 Integration
- Summaries can be generated on demand or automatically
- Summaries are linked to notes and updated as notes change
- UI components can be embedded in note views, dashboards, or toolbars

### 📋 API Endpoints
- POST /api/plugin/ai-summarization/summarize/{noteId}: Generate summary for a note
- GET /api/plugin/ai-summarization/summary/{noteId}: Retrieve summary for a note
- GET /api/plugin/ai-summarization/settings: Get plugin settings
- PUT /api/plugin/ai-summarization/settings: Update plugin settings

### 🧪 Testing
- Validated with sample notes and various summary lengths
- Error handling for empty notes, API failures, and invalid requests
- Responsive design tested on desktop and mobile

---

Closes #27

Ready for review!

This pull request enhances the leaderboard's map visualization by adding a new interactive D3-based visualizer and by providing additional tabular data for the latest solved map. The changes improve both the backend rendering logic and the frontend user experience.

**Map visualization improvements:**

* Added a new D3.js-based interactive map visualizer, implemented in `static/d3-visualizer.js`, which renders rooms and connections with force-directed layout and drag support.
* Updated the backend handler `last_correct_guess` in `src/www/handlers/leaderboard.rs` to embed the D3 visualizer via a `<script type="module">` and pass the map data as JSON to the frontend.

**Tabular data enhancements:**

* In `last_correct_guess`, added two new HTML tables: one showing door connections per room, and another showing adjacency counts between rooms, for improved map inspection.

**Codebase cleanup:**

* Renamed the string variable from `map_html` to `w` in `last_correct_guess` for clarity and consistency.

These changes collectively provide a richer and more interactive visualization of the latest solved map on the leaderboard page.

author: copilot
body:
This PR fixes a compilation error in `LanguageDetectionService.java` at line 175 where the code was referencing a non-existent constant `UNDETERMINED_LANGUAGE` in the ML Kit Language Identification API.

## Problem
The build was failing with the following error:
```
error: cannot find symbol
    if (!LanguageIdentification.UNDETERMINED_LANGUAGE.equals(languageCode)) {
                               ^
  symbol:   variable UNDETERMINED_LANGUAGE
  location: class LanguageIdentification
```

## Root Cause
The constant `UNDETERMINED_LANGUAGE` does not exist in the ML Kit Language Identification API version 17.0.4. The correct constant name is `UNDETERMINED_LANGUAGE_TAG`.

## Solution
- **Fixed line 175 in LanguageDetectionService.java**: Changed `LanguageIdentification.UNDETERMINED_LANGUAGE` to `LanguageIdentification.UNDETERMINED_LANGUAGE_TAG`
- **Updated BuildErrorFixTest.java**: Corrected inconsistent test expectations to use the proper constant name for consistency across the test suite

## Technical Details
- **Correct Constant**: `LanguageIdentification.UNDETERMINED_LANGUAGE_TAG`
- **Expected Value**: `"und"` (undetermined language code)
- **API**: Google ML Kit Language Identification API version 17.0.4
- **Impact**: Minimal change - only the constant reference was corrected, no functional logic changes

This fix ensures the language detection service can properly check for undetermined language results from ML Kit, enabling the fallback to online detection when needed.

Fixes #509.

author: lisanalga-build
body:
This commit introduces a new peer-to-peer task management application built with React Native and the Expo framework.

The application allows users to:
- Create and manage tasks and sub-tasks.
- Mark tasks as complete.
- Star important tasks.
- Schedule tasks with a specific due date and time.
- Assign tasks to other users.

The app uses the `expo-nearby-connections` library for P2P communication, allowing users to share and synchronize their task lists with nearby devices. The task list is persisted locally using `AsyncStorage`.

The UI is built with React Native components and includes modals for adding sub-tasks, scheduling tasks, and assigning tasks.

author: morrisallison
body:
`@noble/hashes` was being used to generate hashes for comparing the contents of style sheets. The plan initially was to replace the package with native `SubtleCrypto` APIs, but on second thought, the hashing was unnecessary altogether. A simple string comparison is sufficient for our use case, so we can eliminate the dependency entirely. 😐 (doh)

The benefit of hashing the contents was to avoid comparing large strings directly, but in practice, it's negligible until the style sheets are megabytes in size, which is highly unlikely when these are typically only going to contain styles for a single component.

BREAKING CHANGE: Removed `hash` property. Style sheet contents are now compared directly as strings instead of using hashes.

author: copilot
body:
The ImGui integration in Rocky's codebase had unguarded references that caused compilation errors when ImGui support was disabled. Several header files included `<imgui.h>` and used ImGui types without proper conditional compilation guards.

## Problem
When building the SDK with `ROCKY_SUPPORTS_IMGUI=OFF`, compilation would fail due to:
- Unguarded `#include <imgui.h>` statements in header files
- ImGui types and function calls not wrapped in conditional compilation blocks
- Missing guards in source files that are always compiled (not conditionally compiled by CMake)

## Solution
Added `#ifdef ROCKY_HAS_IMGUI` guards around all ImGui-dependent code:

**Header files** - Wrapped entire file contents in guards:
- `src/rocky/vsg/imgui/ImGuiIntegration.h`
- `src/rocky/vsg/imgui/RenderImGui.h`
- `src/rocky/vsg/imgui/SendEventsToImGui.h`

**Source files** - Added guards around ImGui includes and functions:
- `src/rocky/vsg/ecs/WidgetSystem.cpp` - wrapped ImGui include and `initialize()` function
- `src/rocky/vsg/imgui/SendEventsToImGui.cpp` - wrapped entire file content for consistency

## Files Already Protected
The following files already had proper guards and required no changes:
- `src/rocky/rocky_imgui.h`
- `src/rocky/vsg/imgui/ImGuiImage.h`
- `src/rocky/vsg/DisplayManager.cpp`

## Result
The SDK now builds correctly whether ImGui support is enabled or disabled. Demo applications continue to work properly through the existing guards in `rocky_imgui.h`.

Fixes #141.
